title: Polymeric platforms and prodrug-based nano assemblies: advancing targeted cancer therapeutics
content: Conventional cancer therapies are often limited by poor drug biodistribution, systemic toxicity, and insufficient therapeutic efficacy. In response advances have been made in pharmacological performance and treatment outcomes. Polymeric carriers enable selective tumor targeting, prolonged circulation, enhanced drug stability, and controlled release. Biodegradable and biocompatible polymers have emerged as particularly promising platforms due to their favorable biological interactions. Prodrug-based nano assemblies provide an attractive solution by enabling high drug loading, enhanced availability, prevention of recrystallization, and controlled release in both time and space. This review provides an integrated perspective on natural and synthetic polymeric systems, emphasizing their structural features, delivery mechanisms, and synergistic potential. This work highlights emerging design strategies and offers guidance to advance polymer-based drug delivery toward effective cancer therapeutics.
